meta.title: Silver City — Pilate Stone Way
meta.subtitle: Carved stones and bone boxes confirm Jesus Christ's world in the dirt.
meta.blurb: Skeptics say Pilate, James, and Nazareth are Gospel inventions with no dig proof. Pilate Stone Way opens the Caesarea Pilate inscription, the James ossuary naming Jesus, and first-century Nazareth houses—ancient archaeology that anchors Jesus Christ's story in real Judea.
meta.notes: Generated from street book. Engine maps lesson fields 1:1 to Learn / Match / Hold / Journal.

learn.shortStory: Diggers at Caesarea found a limestone block with Latin writing. It names Pontius Pilate as prefect of Judea. The stone confirms the Gospel governor who sentenced Jesus Christ was a real Roman official.

learn.hardTeach: Pontius Pilate Stone (Caesarea Maritima, Israel Museum). The block once dedicated a Tiberieum honoring Emperor Tiberius. Its Latin title Prefectus Iudaeae matches the New Testament's Pontius Pilate and shows Jesus Christ stood before a historically attested Roman prefect, not a later legend.

lesson.ideaLabel: A Jerusalem bone box names James, son of Joseph, brother of Jesus.

learn.shortStory: First-century Jews in Jerusalem placed bones in limestone boxes called ossuaries. One box is carved in Aramaic: James, son of Joseph, brother of Jesus. The names match the Gospel family of Jesus Christ.

learn.hardTeach: James Ossuary Inscription (Israel Antiquities Authority). Judean secondary burial in ossuaries flourished from about 20 BC to AD 70. Naming a brother on a bone box was rare and fits a famous relative: Jesus Christ, whose brother James led the early Jerusalem church.

lesson.ideaLabel: Diggers found first-century houses under Nazareth where Jesus Christ grew up.

learn.shortStory: Some skeptics said Nazareth did not exist in Jesus' day. Diggers under the Sisters of Nazareth convent found rock-cut houses, cisterns, and Jewish pottery from the first century. The finds show Nazareth was a real village where Jesus Christ grew up.
learn.mainIdea: Diggers found first-century houses under Nazareth where Jesus Christ grew up.
learn.gloss: Diggers found first-century houses under Nazareth where Jesus Christ grew up.
learn.loci: This idea lives in Pilate Stone Way, with Silas Whitman.

word.sense: the Galilean village where Jesus Christ grew up

learn.hint: Keep the first-century Nazareth houses. Toss the claim that Nazareth was empty until the Middle Ages.
